mechanism.summary: Lazily intern immutable Latin-1 code-unit JsString values within each realm and reuse them only when installing indexed String-box properties. Keep at most 256 entries; non-Latin-1 units use the existing canonical conversion. Both explicit new String and implicit/Object(string) boxing use the same factory. Expected target reduction is 5-15 percent. This removes repeated per-character allocations, not the wrapper source-buffer copy targeted by the rejected sharing unit, and does not virtualize or remove indexed properties.
mechanism.generality: Applies uniformly to every String box without workload/function/key/iteration recognition. The realm owns the bounded cache; ordinary ObjectData, PropertyStorage, frame/binding representation, and generic property semantics stay intact. The cache holds immutable primitive strings only, cannot create realm reference cycles, and copy-on-write preserves independent mutation of derived local values.
semantic_risks: UTF-16 code-unit identity, including Latin-1 non-ASCII characters, lone surrogates and astral pairs
preserving indexed descriptor flags, own-key order and strict/Reflect writes and deletes
copy-on-write must keep pooled values and independent wrappers immutable
realm isolation and bounded lazy memory retention
subclasses, Proxy wrapping and sloppy primitive receiver boxing retain existing semantics

profile_evidence.shared_cost: Current standard-recipe macOS sample records 1120/7166 main-thread samples under the ordinary indexed String-box installation path. This is an inclusive upper bound, not a claim that every sample is removable. Every indexed character currently creates a separate immutable JsString allocation and byte buffer; construction and later destruction repeat for identical code units. Preserve wrapper data, all descriptors and enumeration; share only these immutable leaf values through a bounded realm-owned cache. The workload is amplified only for sampling and never used for formal timings.
